html:
The French campaign in Egypt and Syria led by Napoleon Bonaparte from 1798 to 1801. France hoped to cut Britain's links with India and take a rich province of the Ottoman Empire, which Mamluk beys ruled in practice.

Napoleon landed at Alexandria in July 1798 and beat the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids. Days later the British admiral Horatio Nelson destroyed his fleet at the Battle of the Nile, trapping the army in Egypt. A push into Syria stalled at the siege of Acre in 1799. Napoleon slipped back to France that year and seized power. The army he left behind surrendered to British and Ottoman forces in 1801.

About 160 scholars and engineers came with the army. Their findings filled the huge Description de l'Égypte, and soldiers dug up the Rosetta Stone, which the British took after the surrender. The campaign launched modern Egyptology and a European craze for Egypt. It also broke Mamluk power, which helped Muhammad Ali make himself ruler of Egypt in 1805.
